recipes.name: Johnsonville® Italian Sausage Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package Johnsonville® Italian Ground Sausage

steps.text: In a skillet, cook sausage, onion and garlic until pork is no longer pink and onion is tender; drain. Add marinara sauce and oregano; simmer for 5 minutes. In a bowl, combine ricotta cheese, egg, 1/4 cup Parmesan and spinach.

In a greased 13-in. x 9-in. x 2-in. baking dish, spread 1 cup meat sauce. Arrange 3 noodles over sauce. Spread one-fourth of the ricotta cheese mixture over the noodles, top with 1 cup of meat sauce. Sprinkle with 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese. Repeat process 3 times. Top with remaining Parmesan cheese. Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees F for 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before cutting. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Johnsonville® Italian Sausage Lasagna

author.name: From the Kitchen at Johnsonville Sausage

raw_recipe.description: Johnsonville Italian Sausages make it simple to enjoy authentic Italian flavor. This classic lasagna dish is made so much easier when you’ve got Johnsonville backing you up. The flavor of the Italian sausages will help to make this recipe your new lasagna favorite!

review.reviewBody: Been using this recipe for around 35 years. I use half ground beef and half italian sausage. Also, frozen spinach works fine. If you don't have ricotta cheese use cottage cheese. I've also tried it with swiss cheese on top, then sprinkle parmesan on that and bake. Great recipe, don't think you will be disappointed.

This recipe is great if you use it as a base for making lasagna. I realize this is a Johnsonville recipe, but the ground sausage wasn't sold at the store I went to so I used italian ground turkey (which is healthier anyway) and turned out just as good in my opinion. Also, made my own marinara/basil/red wine sauce. One other thing I changed that seemed to add a little more flavor was I sauteed the garlic and onions separate from the meat/marinara sauce and put them in with the ricotta spinach with a little powdered garlic as well. I'm sure it doesn't matter but I don't like plain layers of ricotta when you get that bite. I flavored my own sauce with oregano so it was in the pasta, not just on top like the recipe says (I would recommend making the sauce with more spices, even if you buy jarred).

Also, add on a few more sprinkles of mozzarella on top about 10 mins before the lasagna is supposed to be done... then leave in the oven for just a tad longer than it's supposed to once you turn the oven off so the italian spices brown a little and the flavors blend (YUM!!!)

The recipe does not call for any seasonings so I added salt, pepper, Italian seasoning and Herbs de Provence. I used Johnsonville Hot Italian Sausage, which by the way is delicious. I did find the lasagna a bit on the dry side, so next time i will double the sauce.
Doubled the garlic, added 1lb of chop meat (85lean/15fat), added 1tsp onion powder, black pepper to taste, parsley to taste, and 1 cup of provolone cheese.

This is a basic, tried-and-true recipe for making lasagna. There are so many ways to change this up if one wishes to. I used the Johnsonville Mild Italian Sausage, which was quite flavorful and melded nicely with the organic pasta sauce that I used. Since I couldn't help myself, I snuck in some slices of provolone between the mozzarella and lasagna noodle layers. It was delicious served with a green salad and home made garlic toast on the side. Treat your family. You won't be disappointed!

This was pretty easy to make. I did read the reviews prior to making and was glad I did. I added extra sausage and extra sauce. I also mixed the ricotta with cottage cheese. It was very good! They even ate the spinach (which they don't like) Will definitely make it again. Looking forward to adding mushrooms to the recipe

Good recipe: I never boil my pasta before assembly. I needed to add more marinara sauce and less ricotta cheese. I would have liked more meat, maybe mix in some hamburger. I used about 1-2 cups STEAMED fresh spinach....frozen would also work fine. I added a row of thinly sliced zucchini cuz I like veggies.

AMAZING! I changed a couple of things to make it spicier. I used spicy ground sausage instead of regular, spicy marinara sauce instead of four cheese and frozen spinach that was thawed and drained. So good!

Big hit in my house. I used Johnsonville Italian sausage and it was delicious. I liked the fresh spinach in it and will add this again. I did add a bit of red pepper flakes to the marinara sauce. I also seasoned my ricotta cheese with fresh basil and parsley. We loved it.

One of my favorite dishes to make for a few days of leftovers. My wife doesn’t like ground meat with pasta so I ha e to be creative, I like to buy Italian sausage strip them out of there casings cut them in half and cook over stovetop until close to done. And than use the links as a layer of meat and just spread red sauce over them. Fantastic treat!! All my coworkers love it! As well as my wife. We can finally have lasagna again.

This was an awesome lasagna! I added mushrooms, green, red yellow and orange bell peppers and used sweet onions in mine, along with mozz and provolone shredded cheese. Made my own sauce and baked two. I got texts/calls VERY quickly about how good this was
Add some seasoning or it will be on the bland side. I did, and it tasted amazing. Good easy starter recipe.
Love this recipe!! It’s mine and my family’s favorite lasagna dish
I added sweet basil and a little more oregano, it was AWESOME!
Delicious!
Very good! It was a little cheesy, and I would love for there to be more meat. Also it could use a little more seasoning and spices, but otherwise this is a great base lasagna!
made it with jarred marinara sauce. Tasted like spaghetti sauce
This lasagna was excellent. I like the Italian Sausage instead of ground beef...more flavorful.

I am a big fan of Johnsonville products, so, thought I would give this a try. I made exactly as the recipe stated. I really liked the creaminess the ricotta gave the lasagna and the spinach was a nice addition. Personally, I thought the sausage taste was a little too much for us for this recipe. Next time I will do have beef and half sausage.
I loved this. My non-eating ricotta family did not give it a fair shake but I loved the depth of flavor that the sausage added.
